messages.content: Find the best local nurseries in Toronto with a good variety of annual plants.

function.name: local_nursery_find
function.description: Locate local nurseries based on location and plant types availability. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city or locality where the nursery needs to be located.

plant_types.description: Type of plants the nursery should provide.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to find local nurseries in Toronto offering a good variety of annual plants. We have a tool `local_nursery_find` which takes parameters:

{
    location: string,
    plant_types: "Annual" | "Perennial" | "Shrub" | "Tree" | "Herbs" | "Fruits"[]
}

We need to call this tool.

But we also might want to ask clarifying question about what exactly they mean by "best". But likely just use the tool.

We'll call it with location="Toronto", plant_types=["Annual"]? Wait type says plant_types can be one of those strings OR an array of "Fruits"? Actually it's defined as `"Annual" | "Perennial" | "Shrub" | "Tree" | "Herbs" | "Fruits"[]`. That means plant_types could either be a single string among Annual etc., or an array of Fruits? That's weird. Probably they meant plant_types: ["Annual"]. We'll pass plant_types: ["Annual"], but maybe better to pass plant_types: "Annual".

Given the schema expects plant_types: "Annual" | ... | "Fruits"[], so if we want only Annual, we set plant_types:"Annual". Let's do that.
